scorecard.note: Clarify and simplify the visual elements so they are instantly understandable on a phone screen; replace vague 'data picture' descriptions with concrete, eye‑catching imagery.

storyboard.ears: A celebrated whale recovery rests on an alarmingly small group of mothers.
The right whale population reached 384. That rebound is real but still dangerously small.
storyboard.eyes: substance: the whale rising free; cause: Data hauls the fishing rope off the whale, one haul per year, and it rises and blows
storyboard.evidence: NOAA Fisheries / Northeast Fisheries Science Center | North Atlantic right whale population estimate | https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/resource/peer-reviewed-research/population-size-estimate-north-atlantic-right-whales | 2026-10-29

storyboard.ears: The latest season produced 22 calves. Every birth depends on the species' limited mothers.
storyboard.evidence: NOAA Fisheries | North Atlantic right whale calves born, 2018 vs recent season | https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/national/endangered-species-conservation/north-atlantic-right-whale-calving-season-2024 | 2026-10-29

storyboard.ears: Only 70 right whales are breeding females. Losing even a few can stall the entire comeback.
storyboard.evidence: NOAA Fisheries | Reproductively active females as a share of the right whale population | https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/national/endangered-species-conservation/north-atlantic-right-whale-calving-season-2024 | 2026-10-29

storyboard.ears: Protecting breeding females is the narrowest path from a fragile rebound to recovery.
